F-2a37 source-assisted re-adjudication, 22 September 2026.
Reader: Codex subagent; exact model identifier unavailable.
Frozen base: review-2026-09-22-image-only.json, captured in commit a574687; unchanged.
Exposure: frozen response, prior report with tentative lemma readings and genre, additional manuscript images, pre-existing processed images, processing scripts, web search results, and a digital Latin text of Augustine Sermo 96. This is assisted work, not another independent reading.

Result: NOT IDENTIFIED / identification confidence none. No sustained distinctive wording has been read and matched. A religious/scholastic commentary remains a catalogue description and plausible working genre, not a recovered title or attribution. Underlining, paragraph marks and initials are visible; they cannot establish the text being commented upon.

Original packet area, n_R0a.jpg, physical rows counted from top, including partial bottom row. The original and cached enhanced view were both inspected:

No secure new continuous reading of this area is claimed. Some isolated shapes could be read differently after exposure to the previous report; none warrants replacing the frozen reading with completed Latin. Row count remains provisional. No deletion/addition can be deciphered securely.

Additional area A: blue-initial passage in u1.jpg, also present near the bottom of c2_R0.jpg, and in overlapping v1.jpg. u1_a.png and v1_ch.png are pre-existing processed renderings of this area, not additional witnesses. Rows numbered within u1.jpg; row1 is the underlined line beside the upper part of the blue initial.
A1 [N?]on[?] est[?] dur[...][?] [...]  (underlined)
A2 filio[...][?] [...] ponit[?] [...] 
A3 [illegible]
A4 [illegible, partial bottom row]
The expansion durum is only a search hypothesis inherited from the prior report; its ending is not recovered securely. Neither the first word nor the decorated letter should be used to identify a biblical lemma. Do not supply non est bonum, discipulus, or another familiar phrase. The possible ponit is a short common word, not a diagnostic anchor. The enhanced versions make strokes darker but do not establish their identities.

Additional area B: red round initial passage, u2.jpg, toward the foot of c2's right column. u2_a.png is a processed rendering. Five provisional rows, including clipped material at the top/bottom:
B1 [illegible; underlined, upper edge partly clipped]
B2 [illegible]
B3 [illegible]
B4 [illegible]
B5 [illegible; lower edge partly clipped]
The prior report tentatively called the initial Q. Its identity and complete lemma are unresolved in this review. No connecting clause recovered. Larger c2_R2.jpg and other lower/left crop inspection did not supply an independently readable continuation.

Provenance correction, kept separate from frozen record: k22-source.json and the frozen packet label n_R0a.jpg as front-cover right upper portion. Visual comparison shows its rows match the upper portion of c2_R0.jpg and the c2.jpg cover, which the inherited report maps to back cover e003. c0.jpg, mapped to front cover e001, is visibly different. Thus the side label is probably wrong. Live Fragmentarium overview/manifest did not load through the web tool, so this audit records the visible overlap and probable side correction rather than pretending to have revalidated canvas metadata. Files and hashes in the frozen record are unchanged.

Search adjudication: quoted exploratory searches used uncertain non est durum, in combinations with filiorum, ponit, hic, commentarium/commentaria, and ad Philippenses. A deliberately alternative non est bonum + ponit search restricted to Corpus Thomisticum did not validate that reading. None yielded a sustained manuscript comparison. Search hits containing common religious phrases are not identification evidence. The digital Latin text of Augustine Sermo 96, section1, was opened at https://www.liriocatolico.com.br/santo_agostinho/obras/sermoes/sermoes_04/sermao-96/ and contains Sed non est durum nec grave followed by an exhortation about fulfilling a command. The manuscript does not yield enough subsequent words to connect it to that passage. Augustine is neither identified nor comprehensively excluded. No other named commentary was textually collated, and no inference of unprinted status follows from the searches.

Scope and tools: functions.exec, exec_command, view_image(original detail), web.run via tools, and collaboration messages. No new image generation, enhancement or rescaling was performed. Existing scripts enh.py, enh2.py, ac.py, ch.py were read to interpret the processed images: channel selection/mixing, local background subtraction and contrast changes, with resizing and in some cases filtering. These are processed copies of existing RGB data, not UV/multispectral acquisitions. Unknown exact crop coordinates and scale persist.

Manuscript inputs displayed: n_R0a.jpg, n_R0a_e.png, c0.jpg, c2.jpg, c2_R0.jpg, c2_R1.jpg, c2_R2.jpg, u1.jpg, u1_a.png, v1.jpg, v1_ch.png, u2.jpg, u2_a.png, u3.jpg, u3_a.png, c0_L2.jpg, c2_L2.jpg, s3.jpg, s3_e.png. Many overlap. The pastedowns and hidden inner face were not inspected in this review. No human palaeographic review. Fresh imaging may improve readability, but its likely success is not established by these RGB images.
